primary_outcome_name: NPRS-Lumbar Pain (Numeric Pain Rating Scale, lumbar back pain)
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: NPRS 0-10 (11-point Numeric Pain Rating Scale, 0 = no pain, 10 = worst pain imaginable), lumbar pain subscale (NPRS-Lumbar Pain), reported separately from NPRS-Leg pain
primary_timepoint: Week 3 (post-intervention, after 10 treatment sessions over three weeks), compared with baseline (pre-intervention)
contrast_reported_primary: Manual Therapy + FMS vs Manual Therapy Only (FMS-augmented group vs manual-therapy-alone control group)
population_detail: Adults aged 18-64 years with MRI-confirmed unilateral lumbar disk herniation with radiculopathy (LDHR), chronic (symptom duration >= 12 weeks; mean ~9.4 months), leg-dominant sciatic pain with a positive Straight Leg Raise test, referred for physiotherapy after evaluation by an orthopedic physician; recruited from two outpatient clinics in Thessaloniki, Greece. Excluded: red flags, bilateral radiculopathy, prior lumbar surgery, recent interventional treatments, contraindications to magnetic stimulation, pregnancy/breastfeeding.

published_estimate.quote: By week 3, however, the FMS group reported significantly lower pain scores compared with the manual therapy group (mean difference = -1.20, p = 0.018, 95% CI: -2.18 to -0.22). The between-group effect size at week 3 was large (Cohen's d = 0.78), favoring the FMS intervention. (Results, Section 3, p. 10; see also Table 3, 'NPRS-Lumbar Pain (score)' row, 95% CI column '(-2.18, -0.22) *', p. 10-11). Primary interaction test reported in the same paragraph: 'A significant group x time interaction was observed for lumbar pain intensity (NPRS-Lumbar), F(1,38) = 8.87, p = 0.005, eta2 p = 0.189 (Table 3), indicating that the two groups improved differently over time.'

B_covariate_list: none used as model covariates. Age, Sex, BMI, symptom duration, affected side and disk-herniation level were compared between the two groups only for baseline-balance purposes (Table 2, independent-samples t-tests / chi-square tests), not entered as covariates in the primary group x time ANOVA.
data_availability_statement: Data Availability Statement: The data that support the findings of this study are openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17936953.
journal: Medicina (MDPI, published on behalf of Lithuanian University of Health Sciences); Medicina 2026, 62, 249; https://doi.org/10.3390/medicina62020249

registry_check.issues: (1) ARM CODING MISMATCH: registry.csv lists arm_control=1, but the deposited SPSS file (Lytras FMS 1 data.sav) defines GROUP value labels as 1.0 = 'Manual Therapy with FMS' (the intervention arm) and 2.0 = 'Manual therpay alone' (the actual control arm). So the control arm is GROUP=2, not GROUP=1 as currently coded in the registry -- this needs correction. (2) COVARIATE MISMATCH: registry.csv lists covars_published='Age,Gender,BMI', but the paper's published primary analysis (two-way mixed ANOVA with only 'group' and 'time' factors) does not adjust for Age, Gender/Sex or BMI (or any other covariate) at all. These three variables (plus symptom duration, affected side, herniation level) are used only for a descriptive baseline-balance comparison in Table 2 (independent t-tests / chi-square), not as model covariates for the primary outcome. B_covariates is therefore coded 'none', not 'published_set'. (3) OUTCOME VAR MATCH CONFIRMED: outcome_var=NRPSLBPpost / baseline_var=NRPSLBPpre correspond to 'NPRS lumbar pain 3rd week' / 'NPRS lumbar pain baseline' in the SPSS labels, which matches the paper's NPRS-Lumbar Pain outcome -- this is one of the co-primary outcomes both in the paper (Methods 2.4: 'All outcomes were considered primary') and in the ClinicalTrials.gov registration NCT07234071 (which lists 'Pain Intensity (NPRS)', 'Straight Leg Raise (SLR) Angle', 'Change in Functional Disability' [RMDQ], and 'Change in Neuropathic Symptom Profile' [S-LANSS] as four co-equal Primary Outcome Measures, with NPRS listed first and covering both lumbar and leg pain). No single outcome is hierarchically primary; NPRS-Lumbar is the first-named/first-discussed of the pain measures in both the registration order and the paper's own subsection order (2.4.1), consistent with the registry's prior choice. (4) The task prompt's working hypothesis that 'FMS' might refer to 'Functional Movement Screen' (suggested by the title wording given in the task) is incorrect for this paper: FMS here stands for 'Functional Magnetic Stimulation', a magnetic-field neuromodulation device applied concurrently with manual therapy -- it is a treatment component/co-intervention, not an outcome measure and not related to the Functional Movement Screen assessment tool.

analysis_method_quote: 2.7. Statistical Analysis: 'All statistical analyses were performed using IBM SPSS Statistics for Windows (Version 25.0; IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA) and R (Version 4.0.3). ... To evaluate the effect of the intervention over time, a two-way mixed-design analysis of variance (ANOVA) was conducted, with one between-subject factor ("group": manual therapy + FMS vs. manual therapy only) and one within-subject factor ("time": baseline vs. week 3). The primary hypothesis test focused on the group x time interaction. When a statistically significant interaction was detected, simple main effects were examined using Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise t-tests. Effect sizes for ANOVA models were reported as partial eta-squared (eta2 p) ... The magnitude of between-group differences was quantified using Cohen's d ... All randomized participants completed the intervention and both assessment time points; therefore, no data imputation was required. Statistical significance was set at alpha = 0.05 for all two-tailed tests. Ninety-five percent confidence intervals (95% CIs) were reported where applicable.' (p. 8-9). Also Section 2.4 (Measurements), p. 4: 'The following measurements were conducted at baseline and after the third week. All outcomes were considered primary and were performed by the same independent assessor, who was blinded to group allocation.'
notes: No single hierarchical primary outcome is designated. The paper explicitly states in Methods 2.4 (p. 4): 'All outcomes were considered primary...' This is corroborated by the ClinicalTrials.gov registration (NCT07234071, fetched directly from the registry API), which lists four co-equal Primary Outcome Measures: 'Pain Intensity (NPRS)' (covering both lumbar and leg pain, pre-treatment/week 3), 'Straight Leg Raise (SLR) Angle', 'Change in Functional Disability' (RMDQ), and 'Change in Neuropathic Symptom Profile' (S-LANSS) -- no single outcome is ranked above the others in the registry entry either. Candidates for 'first-named/most primary' outcome, in order of appearance: (a) Abstract: 'lumbar and leg pain intensity (NPRS), functional disability (RMDQ), neuropathic pain symptoms (S-LANSS), and straight leg raise (SLR) range of motion' -- NPRS (lumbar mentioned before leg) is first; (b) Methods 2.4, subsections in order: 2.4.1 NPRS (lumbar pain introduced before leg pain), 2.4.2 RMDQ, 2.4.3 S-LANSS, 2.4.4 SLR; (c) ClinicalTrials.gov registration order: Pain Intensity (NPRS) first, then SLR, RMDQ, S-LANSS. NPRS-Lumbar Pain is therefore the most defensible 'first-named' choice across all three sources and matches the registry's pre-existing outcome_var=NRPSLBPpost assignment. All five individual outcome variables (NPRS-lumbar, NPRS-leg, RMDQ, S-LANSS, SLR) showed statistically significant group x time interactions (all p<=0.005) favoring the MT+FMS group, with between-group mean differences at week 3, respectively: NPRS-Leg -1.45 (95% CI -2.52,-0.38, p=0.009), RMDQ -3.35 (95% CI -5.64,-1.06, p=0.005), S-LANSS -2.45 (95% CI -4.66,-0.24, p=0.031), SLR +7.10 deg (95% CI 2.70,11.50, p=0.002) -- all favouring the FMS-augmented arm, consistent in direction with the chosen NPRS-lumbar primary estimate. No correction for multiplicity was applied across these five co-primary outcome families (Bonferroni was used only for post-hoc simple-main-effect pairwise t-tests within a given outcome after a significant interaction, not across the outcome family), despite all five being labelled 'primary' -- a notable multiplicity/reporting issue. B_baseline_handling is coded 'other' because the primary hypothesis test is the group x time interaction from a two-way (2-timepoint) mixed/repeated-measures ANOVA -- which is neither a pure endpoint-only comparison, nor an explicit raw change-score t-test, nor an ANCOVA with baseline as covariate -- while the specific numeric estimate extracted as published_estimate (mean difference -1.20, 95% CI -2.18 to -0.22, p=0.018) is itself a Bonferroni-adjusted simple main effect comparing raw week-3 (endpoint) scores between groups, reported after the omnibus interaction was significant. Randomization was stratified by outpatient clinic (2 clinics) using permuted blocks, but the primary ANOVA model does not adjust for clinic/site (B_strat_factors_adjusted='no', B_clustering_modelled='none'). Sample size was pre-specified via G*Power (n=38 required, n=40 recruited); no participant dropped out (100% retention), so ITT = per-protocol here in practice. Funding: 'This research received no external funding.' Trial registered prospectively on ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT07234071); Ethics approval EC-16 2025, IHU Thessaloniki, approval date 5 November 2025 -- note the approval date (Nov 2025) and manuscript received date (14 Dec 2025) are very close together, worth flagging for a general trial-integrity screen but not evaluated further here since that is outside the scope of this extraction task.
